source_text:
Ἀπέχεσθε τῶν κακῶν βοτανῶν, ἅστινας οὐ γεωργεῖ Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, διὰ τὸ μὴ εἶναι αὐτοὺς φυτείαν πατρός: οὐχ ὅτι παῤ ὑμῖν μερισμὸν εὗρον, ἀλλ’ ὰποδιῡλισμόν.
ὅσοι γὰρ θεοῦ εἰσιν καὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὗτοι μετὰ τοῦ ἐπισκόπου εἰσίν. καὶ ὅσοι ἂν μετανοήσαντες ἔλθωσιν ἐπὶ τὴν ἑνότητα τῆς ἐκκλησίας, καὶ οὗτοι θεοῦ ἔσονται, ἵνα ὦσιν κατὰ Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ζῶντες.
μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου: εἴ τις σχίζοντι ἀκολουθεῖ. βασιλείαν θεοῦ οὐ κληρονομεῖ: εἴ τις ἐν ἀλλοτρίᾳ γνώμῃ περιπατεῖ, οὗτος τῷ πάθει οὐ συγκατατίθεται.
thought_title: Stay away from false teachers and follow the bishop
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Philadelphia, warning them to avoid false teachers and to remain united with their bishop.
pass_a_gloss: Keep away from the evil plants, which Jesus Christ does not cultivate, because they are not a planting of the Father. Not that I found division among you, but a filtering. For as many as are of God and of Jesus Christ, these are with the bishop. And as many as, having repented, come to the unity of the church, these also will be of God, so that they may be living according to Jesus Christ. Do not be deceived, my brothers: if anyone follows one who makes a split, he does not inherit the kingdom of God; if anyone walks in another's opinion, this one does not assent to the passion.

choices.why: The rare noun means a straining or filtering out; it contrasts with division, suggesting a purifying separation rather than a full schism.
The participle from σχίζω means to split or tear apart; rendering it as a person who causes a split keeps the active force of the Greek.
ἀλλοτρίᾳ means belonging to another, and γνώμῃ is opinion or judgment; the phrase describes living by someone else's teaching rather than the church's.

choices.english: does not assent to the passion
choices.why: συγκατατίθεται means to agree with or assent to; the passion is the suffering of Christ, and the clause denies that such a person truly affirms it.
rejected: does not consent to the suffering
does not agree with the passion

bible_refs.note: οὐκ ἐφύτευσεν ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ οὐράνιος

pass_b_english: Keep away from the evil plants, which Jesus Christ does not cultivate, because they are not the Father's planting. I did not find division among you, but a filtering out of what is false.
For all who belong to God and Jesus Christ are with the bishop. And all who repent and come to the unity of the church will also belong to God, so that they may live according to Jesus Christ.

Do not be deceived, my brothers and sisters: if anyone follows one who makes a division, that person does not inherit the kingdom of God. If anyone follows someone else's teaching, that person does not share in the passion.

problems.why: Glossary requires 'division' not 'split' for μερισμός/σχίζω related terms; 'split' is banned.
problems.fix: if anyone follows one who makes a division
problems.ruling: σχίζοντι = 'divide'; glossary requires 'division', not 'split'; translation breaches glossary rule

edits.old: if anyone follows one who makes a split
edits.new: if anyone follows one who makes a division

problems.why: ἀποδιυλισμός means 'purification, winnowing' (separating wheat from chaff), not 'separation' as in schism. Ignatius contrasts μερισμός (division/schism) with ἀποδιυλισμός (winnowing/purification). 'Separation' loses the agricultural metaphor and suggests another kind of division.
problems.ruling: Greek ἀποδιυλισμόν denotes winnowing/purification, not generic 'separation'; translation loses agricultural metaphor and changes nuance.

fixed: The English 'a separation' was changed to 'a winnowing' to reflect ἀποδιυλισμός, which means purification or winnowing, not schism.

problems.quote: If anyone walks in another's opinion, that person does not assent to the passion
problems.why: 'Assent to the passion' is opaque; means 'share in' or 'agree with'?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'does not share in the saving power of Christ's passion.'

edits.old: If anyone walks in another's opinion, that person does not assent to the passion.
edits.new: If anyone walks in another's opinion, that person does not share in the passion.

fixed: The phrase 'assent to the passion' was clarified to 'share in the passion' to convey the meaning of συγκατατίθεται τῷ πάθει more naturally.

last_rejected.why: ἀποδιϋλισμός means 'sifting' or 'winnowing out' as separation of wheat from chaff, but 'winnowing' alone is unclear; better 'a sifting' or 'a winnowing-out'.
last_rejected.ruling: "a winnowing" conveys the sense of ἀποδιϋλισμός (separation/sifting) sufficiently; not a meaning change.

polish.changed: Clarified the agricultural metaphor by rendering 'winnowing' as 'sifting,' and replaced the unnatural 'walks in another's opinion' with 'follows someone else's teaching' while preserving the original meaning.

notes.quote: I did not find division among you, but a winnowing
notes.why: 'Winnowing' is positive (separating wheat from chaff), but context suggests testing; reader may miss the agricultural metaphor.
notes.fix: Add note: winnowing separates true believers from false.

notes.quote: If anyone walks in another's opinion
notes.why: 'Walks in another's opinion' is not natural English; the meaning (follows someone else's teaching) is obscured.

polish.changed: Clarified 'sifting' as a positive filtering out of what is false, and made the speaker and subjects explicit throughout.

notes.quote: I did not find division among you, but a sifting
notes.why: 'Sifting' is positive here (like winnowing grain), but modern reader may think of negative 'sifting' (Satan's testing).
notes.fix: Add note: '[a sifting that purifies, not divides]'.
